newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suez chooses Goldman group on loan sales.
newsitem.headline: Suez chooses Goldman group on loan sales.

text.p: French financial group Compagnie de Suez said on Saturday it would pursue talks with a group led by the Goldman Sachs investment banking firm concerning the sale of a portfolio of property loans worth an estimated 4.4 billion francs ($862 million).
Should the deal go through, Suez should turn a profit in 1996, the company added in a statement.
It said its Credisuez unit, after studying the various potential investors, had decided to enter into extended talks with Whitehall Street Real Estate Limited Partnership VII, led by Goldman Sachs.
It said the talks could be concluded within about two months.
Successful completion of the deal "was compatible with a positive consolidated profit for 1996," the firm said in its statement.

With the company's future performance clouded by shaky real estate investments, chairman Gerard Mestrallet appeared last month to back away from earlier assertions that Suez would report a full-year profit for the year.

Mestrallet answered merely "I hope so" when pressed in mid-October on whether the company would be profitable this year. In June, he told the annual shareholders' meeting that "Suez will return to profit in 1996".
At issue in the talks is a portfolio of Credisuez loans made to property developers and market professionals which Suez is trying to sell.
The sale would be "part of the strategy of reducing exposure to property risk by the year 2001," Suez said in its statement.
Among rivals for the deal had been investment groups led by Lehman Brothers and Morgan Stanley.
Suez said it was being advised during the negotiations by the Lazard Freres et Cie investment firm. ($ = 5.105 French Francs)
